newsitem.title: UK: Escape tunnel found at N.Ireland guerrilla jail.
newsitem.headline: Escape tunnel found at N.Ireland guerrilla jail.

text.p: Officers at Northern Ireland's biggest jail for guerrilla prisoners have discovered an escape tunnel leading from a block housing some of the country's leading activists in the campaign against British rule, officials said on Monday.
The Northern Ireland Office said no prisoners had escaped from the tunnel, which was discovered in a routine patrol of the perimeter fence at the Maze jail on Sunday.
The tunnel is thought to have been elaborately constructed and concealed, but it is not known how near it came to breaching the prison's perimeter.

The top-security prison outside Belfast holds about 500 inmates, almost all of them convicted of guerrilla offences in what is one of the largest concentration of guerrilla prisoners in western Europe.
The inmates are segregated into blocks housing republican IRA activists and Protestant guerrillas. The tunnel led into a block housing mainly Irish Republican Army guerrillas.

"It is a very serious incident and is being dealt with appropriately at a high-level conference with senior staff who have met to discuss its implications," said a spokesman at the Northern Ireland Office.
The Maze prison was the scene in 1983 of the largest prison breakout in British history when 38 republican inmates escaped, some of whom are still at large.

The IRA's political wing Sinn Fein was excluded from all-party peace talks on Northern Ireland which started in June last year and which were suspended earlier this month ahead of British national elections on May 1.
